name: Latin American and Latino Studies/Sociology Combined B.A.

paragraphs: Students with a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) in Latin American and Latino Studies (LALS) obtain a multi-disciplinary, global education from the vantage point of the Americas and learn how to make the world a more just place for all. A degree in LALS prepares students to be critical thinkers and engaged global citizens, with core competencies (skills, proficiencies, and expertise) in LALS research, analysis, and intercultural dialogue, all essential for understanding the dynamics of culture, power, and knowledge.

A combined LALS and Sociology B.A. fosters students’ ability to learn from and work with people from a variety of cultures and perspectives, to understand the complexity of current and past societies and social moments, to discover how political, economic, and cultural aspects inform the social, and to use skills from many disciplines and fields.

Sociology is the study of social interactions among individuals and social groups. More specifically, sociologists examine cultural, ideological, economic, and political structures and the processes whereby social institutions are created, maintained, and transformed. The combined B.A. in LALS and sociology allows students to focus their study of sociological contexts and processes within Latinx and Latin American communities.
info_sections.title: Introduction

paragraphs: LALS Program Learning Outcomes:

Critical Thinking. Ability to analyze from a transnational/transborder/translocal perspective—to see the interconnections between Latin American and Latino issues, people, ideas, problems and solutions. This includes key skills, such as understanding sources, comparing arguments, analysis, and historical perspective.

Research Methods. Working knowledge of social scientific and/or humanistic approaches to LALS relevant topics. This includes acquiring qualitative and quantitative skills, gathering or obtaining research data, finding/using primary sources, and other research methods.
Communication. Key communication skills, including written, oral presentation, and digital, including an understanding of media sources and ability to apply media literacy to cross-cultural analysis.

Community Engagement Skills: Acquisition of hands-on skills in collaborative engagement, cross-cultural fluency, and understanding of Latin America and Latino experiences for practical application and engagement with community and civic organizations.
Sociology Program Learning Outcomes:

Critical Thinking: Demonstrate critical thinking skills by analyzing and evaluating social, political, and/or cultural arguments, across a variety of areas such as inequality; social problems; and race, class, and gender.

Sociological Understanding: Demonstrate sociological understandings of phenomena, for example, how individual biographies are shaped by social structures, social institutions, cultural practices, and multiple axes of difference and/or inequality.
Written and Oral Communication: Formulate effective and convincing written and/or oral arguments.
Social Theory: Demonstrate the ability to use several of the major classical or contemporary perspectives in social theory.
Research Methodology: Demonstrate the ability to use several of the major social science research methodologies.

Advising for the combined major in LALS and sociology is available from both advising offices, though the major is housed in the LALS Department.
info_sections.title: Academic Advising for the Program

paragraphs: Students interested in the combined major in LALS and sociology are encouraged to enroll in the one required LALS lower-division course, chosen from LALS 1 or LALS 5 or LALS 10, and the two required lower-division sociology courses, chosen from SOCY 1 , SOCY 10 , or SOCY 15 , at their earliest opportunity.
info_sections.title: Getting Started in the Major

paragraphs: Students planning to apply in this major are not required to complete specific major preparation courses for consideration of admission to the University of California, Santa Cruz.

Students interested in transferring in to UC Santa Cruz as a combined LALS and sociology major are encouraged to enroll in courses that satisfy the lower-division requirements prior to transfer. Visit Assist.org to review transfer articulations and contact advisors for LALS and sociology with any questions.

Transfer students must complete the lower-division course requirements to declare the combined major in LALS and sociology, and should focus on completing these classes as soon as they start at UCSC (if they have not completed these courses prior to transfer). Students should contact advisors for LALS and sociology regarding transferable coursework.
info_sections.title: Transfer Information and Policy

paragraphs: This program does not have a letter grade policy. Major requirements will be met with grades of C or better or Pass, within the parameters of the UC Santa Cruz Pass/No Pass grading policy.
info_sections.title: Letter Grade Policy

paragraphs: The LALS Department encourages students to participate in Global Learning programs whenever possible. Find out more about the programs offered on the Global Learning website or visit their offices on campus, and speak with the LALS undergraduate advisor to learn more about using global learning courses toward degree requirements.
info_sections.title: Study Abroad

paragraphs: Honors are awarded based on the overall GPA in courses taken that can apply toward the major. Honors are awarded to students with a GPA of 3.70 and above. Highest honors are awarded to students with a GPA of at least 3.90, based on a more comprehensive review of their academic work in the major.
info_sections.title: Honors

source.heading: Major Qualification
prose: Students must complete the lower-division sociology courses (two chosen from SOCY 1 , SOCY 10 , or SOCY 15 ) and one LALS course ( LALS 1 or LALS 5 or LALS 10) with grades of C or better or Pass before the major can be declared.

source.heading: Appeal Process
prose: Students who did not satisfy the major declaration requirement but believe there are extenuating circumstances may file a written appeal. Appeals should be submitted to undergraduate advising by sending an email to lalsadvising@ucsc.edu . Students must file the appeal within 15 days of denial of major declaration. The department will notify the student and college of the decision within 15 days of the receipt of the appeal.

source.heading: How to Declare a Major
prose: Students may declare the major through the MyUCSC portal. Any questions should be directed to the LALS undergraduate advisor.

source.heading: Course Requirements
prose: A minimum of 12 courses and one lab are required for the Latin American and Latino studies (LALS) and sociology combined B.A. Students considering a double major or major/minor plan with the combined major in LALS and sociology should contact the LALS undergraduate advisor to discuss their options.

source.heading: Upper-Division Requirements
prose: LALS and sociology combined majors take four upper-division core courses and one writing lab, four 5-credit upper-division electives (two in LALS and two in sociology), and one senior seminar exit requirement in LALS or sociology.

source.heading: Four Upper-Division Elective Courses
prose: Choose two 5-credit upper-division LALS electives (numbered 101-190) and two 5-credit upper-division sociology electives (numbered 110-189).

source.heading: Four Upper-Division Elective Courses
prose: Choose two 5-credit upper-division LALS electives (numbered 101-190) and two 5-credit upper-division sociology electives (numbered 110-189).

source.heading: Disciplinary Communication (DC) Requirement
prose: Students of every major must satisfy a disciplinary communication (DC) requirement. The DC requirement for the LALS and sociology combined B.A. is met by completing:

notes: Option 1: an LALS Senior Seminar (LALS 194 A-Z, excluding LALS 194L) together with LALS 194L; seminar branches enumerate the LALS 194-series courses in the current catalog.
Option 2: SOCY 196S (topics vary; students must apply in advance).

source.heading: Comprehensive Requirement
prose: Students satisfy the Comprehensive Requirement by completing either an LALS Senior Seminar (LALS 194 A-Z, excluding L) and LALS 194L , or complete SOCY 196S . Topics in SOCY 196S vary. Students interested in the SOCY 196S option will need to apply in advance .
